zenithdistance.c: ZENITH Distance, is the Complement of the Sun, or Stars Meridian Altitude, or what the Meridian Altitude wants of 90 Degrees.

zetetickmethodinmathematics.c: ZETETICK Method in Mathematics, is the Analytick, or Algebraiek way, whereby the Nature and Reason of the Thing is primarily Investigated and discovered.

zeugma.c: ZEUGMA, is a Figure in Grammar, when an Adjective, or Verb, agreeing with a ncarcrWord, is also by way of Supplement referred to one more remote. Thus faith Terence, Vtinam ant hiesurdus, aut h.ec tnuta fatta fit.

zocle.c: ZOCLE, is a Square Member in Architecture, being lower than its Breadth, which serves to support a Pillar, or any other part of a Building, instead of a Base, Plinth, or Pedestal. Continued Zpclc, is a kind of continued Pedestal, on which a Structure is raised, but hath no Base, or Cornish.

zodiack.c: ZODIACK, is a Great Circle of the Sphere, dividing it into two equal Parts, cutting the Æqua torn the East and West Points of the Horizon. It cuts the Horizon and Equinoctial obliquely ; making with the former, an Angle equal to the Sun's greatest Meridian-Altitude in any Latitude ; and with the Equinoctial, an Angle of 13° 30 s Minutes, which is the Sun’s greatest Declination. This is a Broad Circle, and thro’ the middle of it is drawn a Line, called the Ecliptics, or Via soli's, the way of the Sun, because the Sun never deviates from it, in his Annual Motion ; as the Planets do all more or less, (whence it hath its Breadth.) The Zpdiack., in the Globe, is mark’d with the Characters of the Twelve Signs, and in it is found out the Sun’s Place, which is under what Star or Constellation he appears to be at Noon. By this are determined the four Quarters of the Year; and accordingly it is divided into 4 Parts, and as the Sun goes on here, he hath more or less Declination, North and South. Also from this Circle, the Latitudes of the Planets and fixed Stars are accounted, from theEcliptick towards its Poles. And those Poles are 2.3 Degrees 30 Minutes di. stant fr j in the Poles of the World, or of the llquinotlial ; and by their Motions are the Polar Circles described. In these Poles all the Circles of Longitude which are drawn thro’ the Zpdiacl do terminate, (as the Meridians and Hour Circles do in the Poles of the World) and as the Azimuth Circles do, in the Zenith and Nadir. The Breadth of this Circle, or rather Zone in the Heavens, is 20 Degrees, for beyond 10 Degrees North, or 1 o Degrees South, the Latitude of no Planet ever reaches. It seems to have been divided into 12 Parts, (which they call Signs) because while the Sun in a Years Time is running thro’ the Zodiack or Ecliptick, there happens to be 12 Lunations : or the Moon undergoes all her Changes and Phases, 12 times, pretty near. Each Sign is divided into 30 Degrees, so that the whole makes 360 : And they begin to reckon at the Eastern Intersection of the Equinoctial and Ecliptick ; or at the Vernal Equinox, where they place the first Point of Aries ; going on thence to Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, &c. and when you count thus forward on according to the usual Order and Course of the Signs, they call it, in constequentia, but if you count backwards from Taurus to Aries, j&c. they say, ’tis in Antecedentia. The Reason of the Name of this Circle, and its Originc was this. Ths Ancient Astronomers observed the Sun in his (apparent) Annual Morion to describe always one and the seme Line or Track in the Heavens, and never to deviate from this Path either to the North or the South, as all the other Planets, they found, did more or less. And because they observed the Sun to shift as it were backwards, thro’ all the Parts of this Circle or Path, so that in his whole Years Course, he would Rife, Culminate, and Set with every Point of it: '1 hey distinguished the Fixed Stars which appeared in or near this Circle into r 2 Constellations or Divisions, which they called Signs, because they were Marks to distinguish whereabout the Sun was. These Signs they painted usually in the form of Animals, and thence came the, Word Zpdiacl^ ; and the very middle Line of it is called the Ecliptick, because the Eclipses only happen when the Moon also is in that Line.

zodiackofthecomets.c: ZODIACK of the Comets, Caffmi hath observed a certain Tract in the Heavens, within whose Bounds (by many Observations) he hath found most Comets, tho’ not all, to keep. This he makes as broad as the other Zodiacs, and marks it with Signs or Constellations like that, which are Antinotis, Pegasus, Andromeda, Taurus, Orion the lesser Dog, Hydra, the Centaure, Scorpion , and Sagittary.

zone.c:
ZONE, in Geography, is a Space contained between two Parallels ; of these Zones there are Five commonly reckon’d, vi\. Two Frozen, two Temperate, and one Burning Zone, The Frozen Zpnes, are those Parts of the Globe comprehended between the Pole and the Polar Circle ; therefore one must be towards the North, the other towards the South : The Frozen, or Frigid Zpne, towards the North, lying between the North Polar Circle, and the North Pole, contains part of Istand, and Norway, Lapland, Finmarl$amojeda, Nova-Zembla, Greenland, and some other Parts of North America. The Frigid Zone, toward the South, lying between the South Polar Circle, and the South Pole, is not yet known whether it contains Land or Water. The Temperate Zpnes are one on the North side of the Equator between the Article Circle, and the Tropick of Cancer ; another on the South side between the Tropick of Capricorn, and the Antartick Circle. Torrid Zpne, or Burning Zpne, contains all that Space of Earth, that lieth between the two Tropicks. zugomaticus.c: ZUGOMATICUS, is a Muscle of the Face, so called by Hjolan, because it arises from the Os Juf nse, or Zygoma. Its Origination is round and 'lcfhy from the external part of the said Bone ; whence descending obliquely forwards, is inserted near the Angle of the Lips. When this Muscle and its Partner act, they draw both Lips upwards, and make a pleasant Countenance.

zygoma.c: ZYGOMA, or Os Mali, is one of the Bones of the Upper Jaw, it is of a Triangular Figure ; on the upper part it jcyns to the Os Sfhenoides, on the lower to the Os Maxillart ; its external part hath a long Process, called ProceJsuS Zygomaticus ; it joyns with the Oj Frontis, at the corner of the Eye.

zygomaticum.c: ZYGOMATICUM, are Muscles which draw both Lips obliquely to either side, and are otherwise called Jugate.

zymoma.c: ZYMOMA, is any Ferment, as the Nitrous Air, the watery Juice in the Mouth, the acid Liquor in the Stomach, the Blood in the Spleen, Bc. Blanchard.

zymosimetre.c: ZYMOSIMETRE, is an Instrument whereby the degree of the Fermentation arising from the Mixture of divers Liquors, is measured ; or the Temperament or degree of heat in the Blood ot Animals, &c,
